headline: Shoot at the earliest remaining right endpoint
statement: Each balloon is a closed horizontal interval [start,end]. One vertical arrow at x bursts every balloon with start <= x <= end. Return the minimum arrows that burst every balloon.
intuition: Sort balloons by their ending coordinate. Shoot at the end of the first uncovered balloon, and use that arrow for every balloon containing that point. The earliest ending gives a position that hits this balloon while leaving as many future balloons covered as possible.
approach: When no previous arrow lies in a balloon, shoot at its end.
Reuse the current arrow for every balloon whose start is <= its position.
correctness: Take a best possible solution’s arrow that hits the earliest-ending uncovered balloon. Moving that arrow right to this balloon’s end cannot lose any uncovered balloon it hit: their right endpoints are no earlier, and their starts were at most the old position. Hence a greedy shot preserves a best possible completion. Applying this exchange repeatedly yields a minimum-arrow solution.
bruteForce: Try candidate endpoint sets and test whether each balloon contains some chosen endpoint; the combinations can be exponential.

complexity.explanation: The end-sorted copy dominates storage and time; one scan tracks the latest shot.

pitfalls: Closed endpoints allow sharing an arrow when start equals arrow.
Use the full integer range; avoid subtraction-based comparisons that could overflow in other languages.
